newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, bucking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, bucking Wall Street.

text.p: Ignoring the Dow's negative tilt, Chilean blue chips rallied to close higher for the first time this week as the market has absorbed a probable increase in U.S. interest rates next week, said dealers.
The bolsa is seen quiet Monday as investors wait for the outcome of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting Tuesday to decide any rates change, they said.
"The market could reactivate on Tuesday and behave normally if the rate change is as expected," said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.
The 40-share .IPSAu index ended unofficially up 1.25 percent at 112.92 points.
The general .IGPAu index gained 0.8 percent at 5,260.55 points amid turnover of 12.3 billion pesos.
Traders noted that investors were taking advantage of the market's slide this week to bargain hunt in anticipation that the market will rally once the rate uncertainty is over.
Several key stocks have moved on the publication of companies' consolidated earnings last week.
Copper products maker Madeco and supermarket chain Santa Isabel lost ground on lower than expected results, said traders.
Flemings downgraded Santa Isabel to hold from buy, citing poor margins in the firm's recently acquired Multimarket chain and pilferage in its Paraguay stores.
Santa Isabel's ADRs ended down 0.95 percent at 26. Madeco lost 1.94 percent to 1,010 pesos.
Winners included bottler Andina, up 2.29 percent at 2,501 pesos, power giant Endesa, up 2.02 percent at 252 pesos and brewery CCU which rose 1.3 percent at 1,560 pesos.
